title: Your system design roadmap
idea: A system design roadmap is the order you grow skills in: clean classes first, then services and data, then trade-offs at scale.
points: You now design classes with SOLID principles, patterns and a full capstone.
Next, practise one low-level design (LLD) problem a week, timed, and explain it aloud.
Then study high-level design (HLD): services, databases, caches and queues.
At work, review designs and write short design notes before large changes.

hero.caption: Each stage builds on the one before. LLD habits carry into every HLD box.

quiz.q: What should usually come right after solid LLD practice?
options: Memorising every Gang of Four pattern by heart
Learning high-level design: services, storage and caching
Skipping design and only grinding algorithm puzzles
Rewriting the capstone in a new language
quiz.why: HLD applies the same skill, splitting responsibilities, at the level of services and data stores. It is the natural next layer.

takeaway: Master the classes, then the services, then the trade-offs between them.
